name: claude-kit
description: Personal Claude Code capability repository: skills, subagents, commands and hooks, packaged as installable plugins.

plugins.name: claude-kit-meta
plugins.description: Install and manage claude-kit itself. Provides /claude-kit-meta:install-here to enable chosen plugins for the current project, /claude-kit-meta:list to see what is available, and /claude-kit-meta:new-plugin to scaffold a new capability pack.

plugins.name: code-graph
plugins.description: Wires the code-review-graph MCP server into delegated reads so 'who calls this', 'what breaks if I change this' and 'what tests cover this' become one deterministic graph query instead of a grep sweep across the repo. Depends on the external `code-review-graph` Python package (`pip install code-review-graph` or `uv tool install code-review-graph`), which this plugin does not install for you. Ships no hooks: the upstream project refreshes its graph on every Write/Edit/Bash call and injects status into every session start, which this plugin deliberately skips in favor of an explicit /code-graph:refresh you run when you want it. Disabled by default because it talks to a locally-run external service that has to be installed and opted into first. It also trims the upstream server's default ~30-tool surface (about 8.6k tokens of schema) down to 9 tools via `--tools`, and excludes the refactor-applying tools specifically because they write to source files, which this read-only pack does not do.

plugins.name: concrete-answers
plugins.description: Forces every answer to name the real thing: a file path with a line, a symbol, the command that was actually run, a business entity, a module that exists in this repo. Bans stand-in labels the user never wrote ($1.1, "step 2", "the module in question") and the filler abstractions that read like a report but cannot be checked ("optimized the logic", "improved robustness"). Also governs how the answer is built: conclusion first and bad news first, verbs instead of stacked nouns, a stated measured-or-estimated qualifier on every number, a recommendation instead of a menu, and a banned list of emoji, exclamation marks and content-free openers. Applies to relayed subagent summaries too: a summary with no file, symbol or number in it is not evidence and does not get forwarded. One resident CLAUDE.md block, one skill for the reasoning, no hooks.

plugins.name: context-trim
plugins.description: Truncates failing command output before it reaches the model, keeping the error context and the tail summary. Leaves clean output intact until it is genuinely huge, and attaches a narrowing tip instead, because cutting a result the agent asked for just makes it run the command again. Also logs per-subagent cost so you can check whether delegating pays off. No agents, no prompting, nothing to remember.

plugins.name: dev-agents
plugins.description: Eleven subagents with the model tier bound per role, so read-only exploration runs on haiku, real design judgement runs on opus, and a gated last resort runs on fable for a problem the opus tier has already failed to solve. Includes a delegation strategy skill that says which agent to pick and how to brief it, plus five reminder hooks: one when the main thread has been grinding alone too long, a pair that asks for a task plan before a subagent is dispatched so a long run plus context compaction cannot lose your remaining steps, one that reads what the dispatch actually returned, so an interrupted, empty or blocked subagent is not mistaken for a finished one, and one that prints the four preconditions before the last resort is allowed to cost you anything.
